producer_report.summary:
I replaced the M20 check that refused any file kind not in the ledger with a check for code in other languages. It flags tracked files by extension (py, js, mjs, cjs, jsx, ts, tsx, sh, bash, zsh, rb, go, pl, php, java, c, cpp, h, lua, ps1) or by a `#!` first line. A line starting `#![` is a Rust inner attribute and is not treated as a shebang. Data and documents (json, toml, yaml, md, txt) pass anywhere with no entry, so a JSON test fixture no longer fails. A named const in xtask/tests/policy.rs lists the two allowed exceptions, `setup.sh` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, each with a reason. The root cause was that the old check judged file format instead of whether the file is code, so it no longer parses docs/non-rust-files.md.

The test `every_tracked_file_is_rust_or_a_listed_kind` is renamed `every_tracked_file_is_rust_or_data_or_an_allowed_exception`. `an_unlisted_file_kind_is_flagged` is replaced by `a_stray_script_is_flagged`. That test checks that tools/build.py, scripts/run.sh, a `#!/bin/sh` file with no extension and a non-root setup.sh are flagged. It also checks that a JSON fixture, md, toml, yaml, txt and a Rust `#![...]` file pass, and that the root setup.sh and the CI workflow are allowed.

I updated the policy.rs header comment and rewrote docs/non-rust-files.md around the new rule and a two-row allow-list table. The notes on git hooks and the absent schemas and gitleaks files are unchanged. The other docs are updated to match:
- docs/enforcement.md row M20 names the new tests.
- decisions.md D33 and its revision note describe the new rule.
- athena-v0.md section 11.3 and the M20 row describe the new rule.
- requirements-map.md row A4-2 mentions the exceptions.
- CHANGELOG.md records the change.

I wrote none of the boundary-scan words in any file.

I confirmed `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked -p xtask` pass. The xtask run covers the new tests plus M19 and M24. I ran the full workspace `cargo test --locked` once but only saw truncated output, so I did not confirm its summary."

checks_run.note: 9 policy tests and 4 unit tests pass, including M19 and M24
Full workspace run completed; I saw only its truncated output and did not read the final summary. The xtask run is confirmed.

open_issues: Extension and shebang detection can miss code in a language not on the list, or in a file with no extension and no shebang. That limit is stated in decisions.md D33.
The allow-list is duplicated in policy.rs and in the table in docs/non-rust-files.md. Nothing checks they match; the docs say to keep them in step.
mistakes: I ran the full cargo test once and did not read its final summary because the output was truncated.
learnings: git ls-files is denied to the producer.
policy.rs already skips owner-private paths through athena_files().
A Rust inner attribute (#![...]) starts with #!, so the shebang check excludes #![.
